AI training jobs: common questions

What is an AI training job?

AI training jobs are paid freelance or contract roles where you help AI labs improve their models: writing prompts and test questions, judging and correcting model answers, annotating data, or building expert tasks in your field. Almost all of them are remote and paid by the hour.

How much do AI training jobs pay?

Each company sets its own rate, and every listing here shows it. Across the hourly roles listed right now, most pay between about $20 and $160 an hour, with a typical top-of-range rate around $80/hr. Generalist work pays least; roles that need medical, legal, finance, engineering or PhD-level expertise pay the most.

Which companies are listed?

Mercor, DataAnnotation, Turing, Meridial, Micro1 and AfterQuery. Listings are pulled from each company's own public job feed and refreshed daily, so the list stays current without anyone re-posting it by hand.

Do I need experience to get an AI training job?

It depends on the role. Many listings want specific expertise, like a degree, a professional license or several years in the field, while generalist and language roles mainly need strong writing and attention to detail. Each company runs its own application and skills assessment.

Is One AI Trainer free, and is it affiliated with these companies?

It is free with no sign-up. One AI Trainer is an independent aggregator, not affiliated with any company listed. Every "Apply" link goes straight to the company's own application page, and some links include a referral code.

Independent listings aggregator. Not affiliated with Mercor, DataAnnotation, Turing, Meridial, Micro1, AfterQuery, or any listed company. Pay and availability set by each company and may change without notice. Application links may include a referral code.
